title: POC Weekly - Variance Sweep & Rerun Plan
summary: Weekly POC sync reviewing INT8/FP8 sweep results. Discussed quality deltas on key prompt sets, latency/throughput tradeoffs, surprising failure modes, and a rerun plan for segmented workloads. Agreed on two benchmark reruns (narrow context vs long form), gating criteria for canary, and security docs to share.
action_items: Maya: run the long-form prompt sweep with new top-k/top-p settings and send results by 2026-10-20
Priya: prepare a trimmed micro-benchmark (50k tokens) showing KV cache warmup behavior for INT8 vs FP8 by 2026-10-18
Alex: share pricing delta table and suggested canary config (routing + fallback) by 2026-10-17
Roberto: validate VPC egress rules and confirm KMS integration constraints by 2026-10-22
next_steps: Schedule rerun window Tue 10/19 02:00-06:00 UTC (off-peak) for long-form sweep
Redwood to provision a temporary dedicated pool for reruns (3x T4 equiv)
Exchange SOC2 report and KMS integration doc link via email
Follow-up check-in 2026-10-22 to review rerun results and decide canary readiness
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-15
Start: 10:30 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (OrbitHealth ML Eng), Roberto Diaz (OrbitHealth Infra), Claire Ho (Head of ML Ops), Samir Patel (Redwood Solutions Eng), Liam O'Neill (OrbitHealth DS)

00:00 Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — results from the INT8/FP8 variance sweep, some odd quality regressions on the Q&A prompts, and then a plan for a rerun segmented by context length. priya is on the call to dig into perf traces.
00:22 Maya: hey, thanks. we pulled the weekly artifacts, we saw the summary sheet you sent (link: https://redwood.internal/poc/orbithealth/sweeps) and some of the deltas are bigger than we expected, especially for the long generative flows.
00:36 Priya: right, to set context: our initial sweep was across three buckets — short context (<=128 tokens), mid (128-512), and long (512-2k) — with INT8 quant (symmetric) and FP8 mix. we observed 2.3% drop in exact-match on short Q&A but a 7-12% SNR drop on long-form summarization for INT8.
01:01 Roberto: that 7-12% is what worries infra — if latency improves but quality regresses that much we can't surface to prod. can you remind us latency deltas?
01:10 Priya: latency improved ~20% p50 and ~15% p95 for INT8 in the short bucket; for long sequences the throughput gains shrink because of KV cache behavior and repeated cache flushes we didn't expect. FP8 had smaller quality impact but less latency gain.
01:32 Alex: and note cost — our estimate sheet shows ~28% per-token cost reduction for INT8 on our hosted footprint but that assumes steady batching; with your request patterns (many short low-latency calls) effective savings are more like 10-12%.
01:51 Claire: so two separate tradeoffs — quality hit on long contexts and cost depends heavily on batching; makes sense. what about rollback and fallback?
02:03 Priya: we have automatic routing rules we suggested — canary a subset via dedicated pool with fallback to FP16 model if a quality regression hits threshold. we can also run hybrid routing: short/latency-sensitive calls to INT8, long-context to FP8 or FP16.
02:24 Liam: on the measurement side, our initial metric was BLEU-ish plus a custom medical-accuracy SNR. is SNR robust? some of the drop might be prompt sensitivity.
02:36 Maya: yes, we instrumented with our clinical prompt set (n=72) and the hallucination score spiked for two types: multi-step summarization and medication reconciliation.
02:48 Priya: that's helpful, thanks. one thing we saw in traces — when the model reaches ~1k tokens the KV cache eviction pattern causes some attention recompute that interacts poorly with quantized kernels; that amplifies small precision errors.
03:08 Roberto: can you show an example trace?
03:12 Priya: sure, uploading now — (brief pause) — ok, look at trace ID rwd-orbit-20261012-324. see at step 256 there's a cache segment switch and a 3-5ms spike that isn't amortized. INT8's quant noise then shows up as a small token selection shift which cascades in long recursions.
03:40 Maya: hmm, so maybe we should avoid INT8 for >1k contexts, or at least use a blended precision for the last chunk.
03:50 Priya: exact. we can do a segmented strategy: FP8 for headroom-heavy long flows, INT8 for short batched endpoints. Also hyperparam tuning — higher top-k or temp tweaks reduce the perceived hallucination.
04:06 Alex: for this week's rerun we propose two experiments: (A) long-form focused sweep with FP8 + tuned top-k/top-p (B) hybrid routing where calls with expected length>1k go to FP8, else INT8. both run on a temporary dedicated pool.
04:25 Claire: ok, practical question — how long will reruns take and will they affect our production?
04:31 Alex: we'll reserve an off-peak window Tue 10/19 02:00–06:00 UTC and spin up a 3-node dedicated pool; should finish within that window. no production impact.
04:43 Roberto: what about security — we need SOC2, KMS and SSO integration docs before we escalate to infra sign-off.
04:50 Alex: yes, we'll send the SOC2 snapshot and the KMS integration guide; Priya will outline our customer-managed key flow and audit log behavior.
05:05 Priya: quick note on KV cache: we can add a transient warming stage in the rerun where we pre-warm common prefixes — that reduces cache eviction noise for long sequences. I'll include that script in the rerun artifact.
05:20 Maya: sounds good. about benchmarks — the spreadsheet you shared had a combined column for "quality delta" across tasks; can we get task-level breakdown? the overall average masks the medication reconciliation regression.
05:32 Priya: absolutely. we'll break out by task and also include the per-prompt seed so you can reproduce locally.
05:40 Liam: also, can we get sample outputs side-by-side? diffs help triage where tokens diverge.
05:45 Priya: yes, sample diffs and per-token log-probs will be included. note though low log-prob doesn't always mean bad, so we'll flag clinical-critical tokens.
05:58 Alex: ok, recapping actions — Maya will run the long-form sweep with updated top-k/top-p by 10/20; Priya will prepare micro-benchmark and warming script by 10/18; Alex shares pricing delta and canary config by 10/17; Roberto validates VPC/KMS constraints by 10/22. we'll reconvene 10/22 to review results and decide canary rollout.
06:20 Claire: last question — our compliance team asked about data residency for logs during reruns. are logs kept in-customer VPC?
06:31 Priya: reruns on the temporary dedicated pool will keep logs in our isolated tenant and we can configure retention; for Private deployments or VPC hostings logs stay in customer-controlled storage. we'll include a short doc illustrating retention settings.
06:48 Maya: thanks all, that's helpful. we'll proceed with the rerun and I'll share intermediate progress in the shared sheet.
06:55 Alex: great thanks, see you on 10/22.

Post-call notes: artifacts shared: rerun plan spreadsheet (https://redwood.internal/poc/orbithealth/rerun-plan-v2), SOC2 snapshot (link to S3), KMS integration guide (doc).
notes: Transcript contains speaker overlap and occasional mis-transcription (e.g., KV cache spelled sometimes as 'k v cache' or 'cache k v'). Some proper nouns may be slightly off.
